chunks: Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abu Shibl, who said:

I and Suleiman ibn Khalid entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). Suleiman ibn Khalid said to him: 'The Zaydiyyah are a people who are known, tested, and made famous by the people, and the most beloved person to them from among those on earth is you. So if you see fit to bring them closer and make them close to you, then do so.' He said: 'O Suleiman ibn Khalid! If these fools intend to turn us away from our knowledge to their ignorance, then welcome to them is not expected, nor are they suitable. But if they listen to our words and await our command, then there is no harm in it.'

key_terms.الزَّيْدِيَّة: Zaydiyyah, a Shia sect named after Zayd ibn Ali
key_terms.السُّفَهَاء: The fools, referring to the Zaydiyyah in this context
key_terms.عِلْمِنَا: Our knowledge, referring to the Imams' divine knowledge
key_terms.يَنْتَظِرُونَ أَمْرَنَا: Await our command, referring to waiting for the Imam's directive

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq view the Zaydiyyah sect and their relationship with the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) evaluates the Zaydiyyah not as a monolithic entity but based on their epistemological orientation toward the Ahl al-Bayt. He distinguishes between the 'foolish' who seek to supplant divine knowledge with their own limited understanding, and those who remain receptive to the Imams' teachings, thereby establishing a nuanced criterion for political and spiritual engagement rooted in the preservation of 'Ilm (knowledge).

en.hubeali: H 14606 – Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Amro Bin Usmaan, from Abu Shibal who said:

‘I and Suleyman Bin Khalid came up to Abu Abdullahasws. Suleyman Bin Khalid said to himasws, ‘The Zaydiites (a sect) are a people who are well known, and tried, and famous among the people, and there is none in the earth who is more praised and more beloved to them than youasws are. So I see that if youasws can be closer to them and bring them closer to youasws, then youasws should do so (lead them as an Imamasws)’. So heasws said: ‘O Suleyman Bin Khalid! If those fools are intending that they would prevent usasws from ourasws Knowledge, to go to their ignorance, then they are not welcome. However, if they had heeded ourasws words, and would have waited for ourasws Command, then there would be nothing wrong with it’.
en.sarwar: 158. Ja’far Bin Basheer, from Amro Bin Usmaan, from Abu Shibal who said:

‘I and Suleyman Bin Khalid came up to Abu Abdullah (a.s.). Suleyman Bin Khalid said to him (a.s.), ‘The Zaydiites (a sect) are a people who are well known, and tried, and famous among the people, and there is none in the earth who is more praised and more beloved to them than you (a.s.) are. So I see that if you (a.s.) can be closer to them and bring them closer to you (a.s.), then you (a.s.) should do so (lead them as an Imam (a.s.))’. So he (a.s.) said: ‘O Suleyman Bin Khalid! If those fools are intending that they would prevent us (a.s.) from our (a.s.) Knowledge, to go to their ignorance, then they are not welcome. However, if they had heeded our (a.s.) words, and would have waited for our (a.s.) Command, then there would be nothing wrong with it’.
